title: Prohibition Signs (Red Circles)
whatItIs: Signs with a red ring tell you what you must not do, such as entering, turning or driving faster than a limit.
keyFacts: Red rings mostly prohibit: the vehicle or action shown is not allowed.
A number in a red ring is the maximum speed.
The white circle with a black diagonal stripe means the national speed limit applies.
'No entry' (red circle, white bar) usually marks the exit end of a one-way street.
A plate below can limit a sign to certain times or vehicles.

a.label: No entry
points: Red circle with a white bar

b.label: No vehicles
points: White circle with a red ring

onTheTest.question: What does a white circle with a black diagonal stripe mean?
onTheTest.why: It's the national speed limit sign. The limit depends on the road and your vehicle: 60 mph for a car on a single carriageway, for example.

traps: The national speed limit sign doesn't mean 70 mph everywhere: check the road and vehicle type.
No entry and no vehicles look alike: one has a white bar, the other is an empty red ring.
Some red-ring signs only apply at certain times: read the plate.
